name: quilm
author: everyday-object semantics (lateral)
description: Matchstick moves on a seven-segment display. Clue: 'X/N', X a 3..6 digit number, N in 1..4. Solution: a number Y of the same length that X becomes when exactly N segments are switched OFF and exactly N are switched ON over the whole display -- 'move exactly N matchsticks and read the new number'. With masks 0..9 = 63,6,91,79,102,109,125,7,127,111 (bits a..g): sum of popcount(Y_i & ~X_i) == N and sum of popcount(X_i & ~Y_i) == N. The two counts being equal means Y lights exactly as many segments as X in total -- sticks are moved, not added. Y must NOT be a rearrangement of X's digits (see below). One-stick single-digit moves: 0<->9, 0<->6, 6<->9, 2<->3, 3<->5, 5<->9, 8->0/6/9 (remove one), 1->7 / 3->9 / 6->8 / 9->8 / 0->8 (add one), so a lone add must be paid for by a removal elsewhere in the number. Intended discovery path: demos show a same-length number differing from the clue in one or two places, with 0<->9, 2<->3, 6<->9, 3<->5 recurring and pairs like (1->7 here, 8->9 there) appearing together; the player has to read the digits as glyphs on a display and N as a count of matchsticks moved. HARDENED FROM v1 (challenges/lab/quilm.v1.json: 'segments added = N', cracked by both Opus players in rounds 4 and 6). v1 was a scalar rule -- property(answer) == clue -- so a fixed answer scanned against every clue read off that property exactly, and 50 distinct clues made memorisation and cross-clue equations cheap. Here validity is RELATIVE to the clue: a constant answer fits only the rare clue it happens to match (measured: all-8s 0.0%, all-1s 0.0%, all-0s 1.2%, random same-length string 0.8%), the clue space is ~10^k x 4, and the balanced on/off counts kill every v1 shortcut (all-8s, x='1'*k, and anything that only adds segments). The non-rearrangement clause closes the one blind family the audit found: permuting X preserves its segment total for free, so 'clue reversed' / 'clue sorted' / a random permutation scored ~11% with no insight at all and handed out labelled equations; with the clause they score 0%. Other witnesses closed: empty, the clue, the clue's digit part (0 moves), any single symbol, Y=X. PRIVATE.
